descriptionChirho: Causative active scattering: God or an agent disperses people, nations, or objects — Arabic بَدَّدَ/شَتَّتَ (Form II), Korean 흩으-/흩뜨리- (transitive), Swahili -tawanya (transitive).
Passive or middle-voice scattering: the subject is scattered or found in a scattered state — Arabic تَشَتَّتَ/تَفَرَّقَ (Form V), Korean 흩어지- (intransitive), Swahili -tawanyika (stative/passive).
Basic intransitive scattering: subjects scatter or disperse of their own accord — Arabic تَفَرَّقَ/تَبَدَّدَ, Korean 흩어지-, Swahili -tawanyika; includes Qal passive participle 'scattered ones'.
Reflexive breaking or shattering — semantically distinct from scattering; Arabic تَفَتَّتَ 'crumble', Korean 부서지다 'be broken', Swahili -vunjika 'be shattered'.
